subject: Discovery Recap: Reducing Inference Unit Cost & Ops (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finbot.ai>, Lena Park <lena@finbot.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Reducing Inference Unit Cost & Ops (FinBot)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid conversation about where FinBot is seeing pressure on inference economics. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Token/unit cost is the single biggest constraint for new product features (real-time scoring on incoming transactions).
- Current infra is a mix of PyTorch -> Triton + some in-house batching; you’re seeing uneven utilization and spiky costs.
- Limited ability to safely quantize some models due to accuracy sensitivity on fraud edge cases.
- Ops overhead: model rollouts and rollback are manual; need graceful fallbacks for peak traffic.

Current stack & constraints we noted:
- Serving: on-prem GPU fleet + cloud burst to GCP.
- Inference path: PyTorch models exported to Triton, some TensorRT usage for a subset of models.
- Latency target (p99): <= 120ms for scoring path; typical request payloads are 80–150 tokens.
- Throughput: 2–5k requests/minute during peak windows, with occasional spikes to 10k.

Success criteria for a pilot (what will make this successful for FinBot):
1) 2x reduction in $/1000 tokens (unit economics) for the scoring pipeline at production traffic profile.
2) Maintain p99 latency <= 120ms.
3) Seamless canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models or different regions during capacity pressure.
4) Clear measurement dashboard (per-route cost/latency) and a plan for integrating with your internal monitoring.

Technical specifics we discussed (and what we’d like to confirm):
- Batching/caching: You’re willing to try increased batching and prefix/KV caching for scoring requests where cache hit rates are expected (session / recent-customer contexts). We estimated this could cut per-token cost by ~20–40% depending on hit rate.
- Quantization: Team is open to 8-bit quantization for non-sensitive models but wants an evaluation plan for the fraud-sensitive model family (A/B quality tests).
- Model variants: You have a smaller distilled model in staging that could be used as a fallback for high-throughput windows.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Tech deep-dive (60m) with Vivek and your infra lead to map exact inference flow, Triton configs, and batching windows — propose Wed Jul 2 or Thu Jul 3, 10–12 PT.
- We’ll share a tailored pricing/throughput worksheet for your workload by EOD tomorrow (redwood-pricing-worksheet.csv).
- Agree pilot scope: a 4-week focused pilot on the real-time scoring route covering quantization experiment + batching/caching changes and dashboarding.

Deliverables from Redwood for pilot
- Performance plan: recommended batching sizes, KV/prefix cache suggestions, and quantization profile options.
- Cost model: expected $/1000 tokens under three scenarios (baseline, batching+cache, batching+cache+quantization).
- Rollout playbook: canary steps, monitoring guardrails, rollback triggers.

Can you confirm:
1) Which date/time works best for the tech deep-dive (Wed Jul 2 or Thu Jul 3)?
2) Who from your infra team should join (name/email) so we can include them on the invite?

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet.csv (we’ll send initial numbers after we sync infra details).

Thanks — excited to help drive down unit costs while protecting accuracy on your sensitive models.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finbot.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Reducing Inference Unit Cost & Ops (FinBot)

Great recap — thanks Marissa. Couple of clarifications and a few details from our infra/ops side:

Clarifications:
- Latency: the strictest SLA is the fraud synchronous scoring path where p99 must be <= 120ms; for feature enrichment/background scoring we’re ok with higher latency.
- Model sizes: production model (fraud-main) is 7B, distilled candidate is ~1.2B. We can tolerate some quality delta on background models but not on fraud-main.

Infra specifics:
- Serving: Mostly Triton with a small set of TensorRT-optimized models. We also have a sidecar caching layer that holds recent KV entries but hit rate is only ~18% currently.
- Request distribution: 75% of requests are short (<60 tokens) for quick decisions; 25% are longer scoring contexts.

Quantization openness:
- We are open to exploring 8-bit dynamic quantization for fraud-main if we can validate end-to-end quality (precision at top-N metrics) in a controlled rollout.
- For the distilled model we’re open to more aggressive quantization and kernel-level optimizations.

Pilot ask:
- We’d like Redwood to run the batching/caching experiment on a shadowed copy of the scoring traffic first, and run an offline quantization A/B on a labeled holdout set.

Attachments: FinBot_SLA_Request.pdf (procurement asked us to gather these items).

Tech deep-dive: Thu Jul 3, 10:30–11:30 PT works best for our infra lead (Carlos Ramos, carlos@finbot.ai). Can you send an invite?

—
Alex Johnson
Head of Product | FinBot Analytics
alex@finbot.ai | +1 (206) 555-0987
